result.dimension: Clock data cleared on duplicate / reschedule (fix list #2, P0)
result.summary: DUPLICATION IS FIXED; RESCHEDULE IS NOT. Duplicating a job that carried a live clock-in produced a completely clean copy (no clockInTime, no work session, no clocked-in state, no time-tracking row). Rescheduling did NOT clear anything: an IN_PROGRESS job with a live clock-in was moved from Sep 10 12:00 PM to Sep 18 12:00 PM through the admin job edit form, the date moved, and every clock field survived — Job.clockInTime, Job.lateArrivalAt, the open JobWorkSession, JobAssignment.status=CLOCKED_IN + its clockInTime, and the status stayed IN_PROGRESS instead of reverting to SCHEDULED. /admin/time-tracking then showed a phantom live shift: "CURRENTLY CLOCKED IN 2 ... Job #5 · ZZTEST Cap OK Client · Sep 18, 2026 · In: 4:48 PM · Out: — · 10m elapsed" — a shift ticking on a job dated 8 days in the future. This is exactly the scenario src/lib/job-reschedule.ts says the fix exists to prevent. The clearing branch never ran: /admin/logs has no "clock-in data was cleared" row at the save time and dev.log has no "[saveJob] clearing the clock trail failed" line, so it failed silently rather than throwing. Confirmed in the UI and by two read-only DB reads 2 minutes apart, so this is not an early read. Separately, rescheduling a COMPLETED job also preserved everything, which the helper documents as deliberate (SETTLED = COMPLETED/PAID are exempt) — reported as scope, not as a defect.

result.summary: Fix #13 holds up on the admin half. /admin/announcements renders, an admin can publish, pin/unpin, edit and delete, and the read-tracking that the phrase "with admin visibility" promises genuinely exists: every card carries an admin-only "Seen by N · M not yet" disclosure that expands into named Read entries with timestamps, named Reacted entries with emoji and timestamp, and a "Not seen yet" list. I drove the whole loop end to end: published "ZZTEST announce 015508" (pinned) as ZZTEST Owner → it showed "Seen by 0 · 3 not yet" → cleaner1 and cleaner2 each saw the "New" chip and a sidebar badge "Announcements 1" → reading cleared both → the admin card then read "Seen by 3" listing "ZZTEST Cleaner One Sep 11, 2:08 a.m." and "ZZTEST Cleaner Two Sep 11, 2:14 a.m.". Cleaner1's 🎉 reaction surfaced admin-side as a "🎉 1" count on the card, "REACTIONS 2 from the crew" in the header stat, and "Reacted · 🎉 ZZTEST Cleaner One · Sep 11, 2:19 a.m." in the panel. Edit and delete both propagated to the cleaner feed. Cleaners correctly get NO read register of their colleagues. Two soft spots, both minor: editing an announcement leaves everyone stamped as having "Seen" content they have never seen (no chip/badge returns), and the author is auto-counted as a reader of their own post. Compose is deliberately spartan — title, message, pin. There is no targeting (all vs specific cleaners), no tagging/category, no scheduling, and the reaction set is fixed at 👍/🎉/❤️. Pace note for whoever reads this: publish took 162–175s and edit 72s to commit; every judgement below was taken after the modal closed on its own. Unrelated background noise seen on admin pages: repeated 500 from http://zztestqa.localhost:3006/api/presence/ping. result.summary:
Shift drop notifications work, and the same-day case is genuinely handled differently — I proved it by real clicking, not by reading source.

Setup gotcha worth recording for anyone repeating this: the store runs America/Toronto while this machine runs IST, so a job the admin date picker calls "today" can still be more than 24h away in absolute terms. My first "same-day" job (Sep 11 9:30 PM) was really 29h out and behaved as a normal drop. I recomputed against the browser clock (2026-09-10T21:19Z) and built job #16 for Sep 11 8:00 AM (~14h out) to get a true late cancel.

What the cleaner sees: a "Can't make it?" card on the job detail page whose static sub-line always warns "Cancelling less than 24 hours before the shift incurs a 1-star penalty.", plus a "Cancel shift" button. Clicking it swaps in an inline confirm panel (no modal). Beyond 24h the panel says only "Are you sure you want to cancel this shift? This cannot be undone." with [Keep shift] [Confirm]. Inside 24h it adds a red line "Late cancellation: A 1-star penalty will be applied." and the primary button becomes "Cancel anyway". Both end with green "Shift cancelled." text after 86-144s — the long wait is normal here, the modal not closing yet is not a bug.

The documented urgent difference is real, with three independent tells: the cleaner-side warning and button label; two admin rows instead of one at /admin/notifications ("ZZTEST Cleaner One dropped a shift" amber/WARN plus "Cover needed — ZZTEST Client Alpha in 14h" red/ERROR, both on job #16); and three email-skip lines in dev.log inside the 118s cancel request versus exactly one for the >24h drop. Admin in-app records: confirmed present and correctly linked for all three drops, with the page's own promise holding — "kept here even when the matching email is switched off."

Pool repost: confirmed. Jobs #12, #14 and #16 all appear on cleaner2's /cleaners/available-jobs with "1 spot remaining" and "Claim this job".

One minor finding: the skipped email is not identifiable anywhere. dev.log emits only the generic "[email] RESEND_API_KEY is not set — emails will be skipped" with no key, recipient or subject, and sendAdminShiftDropped calls deliver() without a logId so no EmailLog row is written either — meaning a real admin has no way to confirm the urgent cover email went out. I could only distinguish the two paths by counting undifferentiated lines.

One item BLOCKED: I could not see the "LAST MIN · +$10" broadcast invite on cleaner2's My jobs. Those invites expire after 10 minutes (scheduling.acceptDeclineTimeoutMin default 10) and my first read was outside it; the two-browser retry hit a 500 (PrismaClientKnownRequestError on db.organization.findUnique) under concurrent load and that drop never committed — confirmed by the absence of any notification row for it. results.item: BUG A — post-create redirect to /admin/jobs renders the public Awer signup page
results.expected: After Create Job, the browser lands on the admin Jobs list at http://zztestqa.localhost:3006/admin/jobs
results.actual: URL is http://zztestqa.localhost:3006/admin/jobs but the page rendered is /get-started — title "Start your workspace · Awer", h1 "Start running your cleaning company.", plan cards Starter $49 / Professional $149. A hard reload of the same URL renders the real jobs list.
results.whatIDid: Signed in as zztest-owner, filled /admin/jobs/new (clientName ZZTEST KnownBugs Client A/B/C, date, time, price, 2 cleaners), clicked Create Job, and captured every request/response header plus framenavigated events. Reproduced 3/3. Then read the dev server log and ran a control curl against the bare host.
results.whatISaw: 3/3 reproductions. Network: POST /admin/jobs/new (next-action) → 303 with `x-action-redirect: /admin/jobs;push` (the Location is a bare path — the redirect does NOT lose the subdomain). The very next request the router makes is POST /admin/jobs carrying `next-router-state-tree: ["",{"children":["get-started",{"children":["__PAGE__"…` — i.e. the flight payload returned by the 303 was already the get-started tree, and the browser then pulls /_next/static/chunks/src_app_get-started_page_tsx_89150cbe._.js. dev.log shows, immediately BEFORE the POST: ` GET /get-started 200 in 96ms (compile: 15ms, proxy.ts: 7ms, render: 74ms)` — proxy.ts ran on an internal request and that request ended at /get-started. WHY: Next re-renders the redirect target inside the action request, that internal request does not carry the tenant Host, so orgSlugFromHost() (src/lib/tenant.ts, `if (parts[parts.length-1]==="localhost"){ if (parts.length < 2) return DEFAULT_ORG_SLUG; …}`) returns DEFAULT_ORG_SLUG === PLATFORM_ORG_SLUG ("platform"), and the guard in src/proxy.ts `if (orgSlug === PLATFORM_ORG_SLUG && !isPlatformPath(pathname)) return redirectSamePath(request, '/get-started')` fires. Control: `curl -i http://localhost:3006/admin/jobs` → `307 Temporary Redirect, location: /get-started` — the exact branch. So the answer to the question asked is: NOT the Location header, and NOT the redirect in page.tsx — tenant resolution picks the platform org on the internal re-render. Blast radius: this is generic to any server-action redirect, not just job creation. Files: src\proxy.ts (platform guard + host-only resolution), src\lib\tenant.ts (orgSlugFromHost → DEFAULT_ORG_SLUG fallback), src\app\admin\jobs\new\page.tsx:950 and :970 (the redirect that triggers it).

results.item: BUG D — cleaner rating differs between /cleaners/dashboard and /cleaners/my-pay

results.whatIDid: NOT blocked — zztestqa does have rating data. Signed in as zztest-cleaner1 (door /cleanos/login), loaded /cleaners/dashboard, read the performance tile, then loaded /cleaners/my-pay in the same session and read the rating banner. Then traced both calculations in source.
results.whatISaw: Dashboard text: "Performance 1.0 / 5 Based on 2 reviews JOBS DONE 1 UPCOMING 6". My-pay text: "Your Rating: 4.0 / 5.0 Based on customer feedback and performance". THE TWO CALCULATIONS: (1) /cleaners/dashboard re-exports /admin/dashboard/page.tsx which renders CleanerDashboard.tsx — src\app\admin\dashboard\CleanerDashboard.tsx:106-111 loads employeeRating rows `where:{employeeId,excludedAt:null}, take: 30` and :177-179 computes a plain mean `ratings.reduce((s,r)=>s+r.rating,0)/ratings.length`, null when there are none, printed at :355 as `avgRating.toFixed(1)` with "Based on N reviews" at :358. (2) /cleaners/my-pay/page.tsx:29 calls getEmployeeAvgRating (src\app\admin\actions\setEmployeeRating.ts:37-50) which averages ALL non-excluded rows (no take limit), clamps to RATING_MIN 1.0 – RATING_MAX 5.0, and returns DEFAULT_STARTING_RATING = 5.0 when there are none — then MyPayClient.tsx:226 re-clamps FOR DISPLAY with `Math.min(5, Math.max(4, Math.round(starRating*10)/10)).toFixed(1)`, a hard floor of 4.0, and the star row at :234 does the same. THREE ways they diverge: (a) the [4,5] display floor on my-pay — the dominant one here, turning a true 1.0 into 4.0 and a reported 3.3 into 4.0; (b) take:30 vs unlimited, so an 31st-oldest rating counts on one page and not the other; (c) zero ratings → dashboard "—"/"No reviews yet" vs my-pay 5.0. Matters beyond cosmetics: src\lib\pay-tiers.ts keys the Standard band (40–45%) off rating, so the number the cleaner is shown is not the number that pays them.
